Messages.Author: David Oros
Messages.Body:
Here is my early morning, no coffee, stayed up all night grading rant
about the new colours, it is in no way well written, or even well
composed, the spelling and grammar usage is abyssmal, but the feeling
I take credit for,
David

Hello,

I am disappointed that none of the questions about Set
layout were covered in the Developer Chat. I don't know if
that is Conrad or Steve's fault.

Steve,

I appreciate the attempt to help fix up the cracks and
corners in VTES, I thank you for all efforts to make the
game more accesible to new people. I *like* the new
layout. I HATE the new colours, they are awful.

I am sure you need no reminder that this game will live
with or without White Wolf, although I know we all prefer
to have you guys making new cards and employing LSJ and his
wisdom. BUT why, why didn't you get a larger sampling of
opinions about the new cards? Why didn't you guys make
sure the colours came out before printing so many? I mean
White Wolf is a professional company now, no more
excusses. This Sh*t was tolerated in 92,93, 94 when you
guys were "the Renaissance in games", but you(and your Bro)
have been doing this stuff for what 13+ years now?

Its poor form, dodging the questins in the Chat the other
day was worse. This game is played because people love it,
please talk to the community that is supporting your
company.

Imagine if this was a new game, do you really think you
have done enough to sell it on its own? I doubt it, WE do
the work for you guys, treat us with more respect.

David Oros

Messages.Author: Geemarcus
Messages.Body:
I'll add my support and agreement to you, as you seem to be taking
some flak here. The cards really tend to all look the same, which
I've complained about before... This is due not only to the colors,
but the layout, which I'm still trying to like, but the more I play
with them the less I like...

One thing I haven't seen mentioned is the generally poor quality of
the printing I've noticed so far. Why the flat finish to the cards
instead of glossy? And many cards look particularly poor. Every time
I pulled a Taste of Vitae I cringed, has this picture always looked so
blurry?

Many of the Vamps seem very cartoony, lending creedence to the idea
that this is a "Portal" version of VTES. If that's the case, just say
so, and go back to the dark, original version for subsequent
"advanced" sets. I simply can't imagine these cartoony versions of
most of the BL clans, for example.

And while I'm at it, I'll add that while I really like a lot of the
new artwork, a lot of it is just poor, and they should have stuck to
the originals (Majesty, for example). And I really wish they'd used
the Sabbat version of the Thau master, I've only got one of those.

Just my 2 cents. Hey, it's only a game... Still love it!

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <20020824000533...@mb-fy.aol.com>, Halcyan 2

<halc...@aol.com> writes:
>BTW: Did I mention that Conrad accused me of being argumentative? Remember when
>someone asked about the Lasombra Antitribu and LSJ replied that there aren't
>enough !Lasombra for them to be considered a clan? Well, being the smart-ass
>that I am, I followed with a question "Well, if there aren't enough Lasombra
>Antitribu to make them a clan, why is there a clan Salubri?"

Random answers:

- that the Lasombra Antitribu are merely Lasombra who split off from the
clan, rather than a whole tribe of them creating progeny as a
self-sufficient sect

- that it was felt Lasombra Antitribu childer should automatically be
claimed back by the Lasombra clan and Sabbat sect (a new clan
would have its own default sect, probably Independent or
Camarilla)

- that, as Bloodlines was marketed heavily as a "Here's lots of vampires
you can screw around with but they aren't viable on their own",
'clans' of three or five vampires were felt appropriate for it.
In a Normal Set (tm), clans would have to be viable on their own
footing. ("Buy this new set to get a playable new clan! And,
err, some not playable clans too! Erm, we're not sure what his
is!")

- extensive playtesting suggested that Salubri and !Salubri together
would be unbalancing (e.g. 8 vampires counting for
Consanguineous Boon)

- that cards such as Blessing of the Name were already sketched in, and
having another three vampires able to play it was considered
detrimental to balance

- that the clans Salubri and Salubri Antitribu are far more distinct
than Lasombra and Lasombra Antitribu. The use of Valeren and
Obeah, for instance, rather than identical clan disciplines

- Sight Beyond Sight was felt to be balanced by it requiring, currently,
vampires of 5, 6 or 7 capacity to bring out. Playing it on a
two cap was felt unbalancing

- that a significant downside for balacing the !Salubri is that they
have to go outside of their own clan for any usable amount of
superior Auspex and superior Fortitude

--
James Coupe

Erm...well.

Put bluntly, the cones and rods in our eyes all differ.
For me, all the cards looked almost identical.

I'll postface with the fact that I'm
color blind to an extent.

Finally, I'll postface the previous statement with this:
All the cards from V:TES on all STAND OUT. I can EASILY
tell the Malks from the Brujah from the Tremere.

I could EASILY tell the master cards from the action
cards from the reaction cards. I reveled in the fact that
most all of the cards were easily distinguishable from
the others whether it was card type or vampire type.
Hell...I even remember way back in my young days
when first playing Magic. It was somewhat easy to
tell red, blue, and black cards apart.

NOW....now it's much more dificult for me to
differentiate the cards apart in the Camarilla
Edition. I was somewhat saddened at the effort
I had to put forth in telling the vampires
apart clan-wise cross table. This was a problem
I never experienced before. And the master
cards?

I know you've heard this all before, but I'm adding
to the discussion. I may be the minority with my
vision disability but that isn't a small minority,
I assure you. Where once I was extremely pleased
with the ease of play and eye-friendliness of
V:TES, now I'm somewhat discouraged with the cards.
(As well as a noxious chemical odor from the cards...
I posted something else about this already)

I have to give a thumbs down to the design team
when it comes to color for this Camarilla expansion.

-Shawn D

Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:


Everyone who comments on CCG playtesting should see what it's actually like
sometime. When done right, it's a tedious, unpaid job constrained at times by
factors completely out of the playtesters' (and, sometimes, the designers' in
the case of licensed games) control.

Most frustrating activity I've ever done for a CCG company. (Art requests were
less enjoyable but not as frustrating.)

Do have to feel your way through at times because there aren't enough in house
playtesters and the volunteer playtesters aren't professionals. I increasingly
wonder how CCGs work as well as they do.
